content.name: Content
content.value: This strand focuses on students applying the seven transferable skills in language and literacy contexts, developing digital media literacy skills, applying language and literacy learning in other contexts, and engaging with texts that foster understanding of diverse identities, experiences, perspectives, histories, and contributions. In all grades of the language program, the learning related to this strand takes place in the context of learning related to Strand B, Foundations of Language; Strand C, Comprehension: Understanding and Responding to Texts; and Strand D, Composition: Expressing Ideas and Creating Texts. Strand A should be assessed and evaluated within these contexts.

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of how the seven transferable skills (critical thinking and problem solving; innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship; self-directed learning; collaboration; communication; global citizenship and sustainability; and digital literacy) are used in various language and literacy contexts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify how transferable skills can be used to support communication in various cultural, social, linguistic, and domain-specific contexts, and apply them when reading, listening to, viewing, and creating texts of various forms

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of how transferable skills help them to express their voice and be engaged in their learning

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate and apply the knowledge and skills needed to interact safely and responsibly in online environments, use digital and media tools to construct knowledge, and demonstrate learning as critical consumers and creators of media

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of their rights and responsibilities when interacting online with appropriate permission, and make decisions that contribute positively to the development of their digital identity and those of their communities

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of how to navigate online environments safely, manage their privacy, and interact in a way that supports their well-being and that of others, including seeking appropriate permission

content.name: Content
content.value: gather, evaluate, and use information, considering various perspectives, to construct knowledge and demonstrate learning

content.name: Content
content.value: apply language and literacy skills in cross-curricular and integrated learning, and demonstrate an understanding of, and make connections to, diverse voices, experiences, perspectives, histories, and contributions, including those of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit individuals, communities, groups, and nations

title.name: Title
title.value: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Perspectives and Ways of Knowing

content.name: Content
content.value: identify themes explored in First Nations, Métis, and Inuit cultures to demonstrate an understanding of the varied identities, perspectives, relationships, legacies, truths, and ways of knowing, being, and doing

content.name: Content
content.value: apply listening, speaking, and non-verbal communication skills and strategies to understand and communicate meaning in formal and informal contexts and for various purposes and audiences

content.name: Content
content.value: use effective listening skills, including listening attentively and asking relevant questions, in formal and informal contexts, including conversations and classroom activities

content.name: Content
content.value: identify and use listening strategies before, during, and after listening to comprehend information communicated orally and non-verbally

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the purpose and audience for speaking in formal and informal contexts, and use appropriate speaking strategies, including taking turns, understanding when to speak, and knowing how much to say, to communicate clearly and coherently

title.name: Title
title.value: Language Foundations for Reading and Writing

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of foundational language knowledge and skills, and apply this understanding when reading and writing

content.name: Content
content.value: use understanding of the sound structure of spoken words to orally isolate, blend, and segment phonemes, from simple structures with two phonemes to structures with more phonemes

content.name: Content
content.value: name and form the upper- and lowercase letters both in and out of order and demonstrate knowledge of alphabetic order, with automaticity

content.name: Content
content.value: identify, read, and spell most common grapheme-phoneme correspondences of consonants and vowels, with automaticity

title.name: Title
title.value: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Phonics Knowledge

content.name: Content
content.value: use phonics knowledge and phonemic blending to read words, and phonemic segmentation to spell phonetically regular words, in isolation and various text contexts

title.name: Title
title.value: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Orthographic Knowledge

content.name: Content
content.value: use developing orthographic knowledge, including position-based tendencies, to make a spelling choice or accurately pronounce a word when reading

title.name: Title
title.value: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Morphological Knowledge

content.name: Content
content.value: use developing knowledge of the meanings of words and common morphemes (i.e., bases, prefixes, and suffixes) to read and spell words

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of commonly used words, acquire and use explicitly taught vocabulary in various contexts, including other subject areas, and use their developing morphological knowledge to analyze and understand new words in context

title.name: Title
title.value: Reading Fluency: Accuracy, Rate, and Prosody

content.name: Content
content.value: read simple words, short sentences, and paragraphs in a variety of texts fluently, with accuracy and appropriate pacing to support comprehension, and read aloud with expression

title.name: Title
title.value: Language Conventions for Reading and Writing

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of sentence structure, grammar, cohesive ties, and capitalization and punctuation, and apply this knowledge when reading and writing sentences, paragraphs, and a variety of texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify and construct simple and compound sentences, including declarative, imperative, interrogative, and exclamatory sentences

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the functions of parts of speech in sentences, including common singular and plural nouns, using the pronoun “I”, the past, present, and future verb tenses, common adjectives and adverbs, and common conjunctions, and use this knowledge to support comprehension and communicate meaning clearly

content.name: Content
content.value: use their understanding of the meaning and function of capitalization and punctuation to communicate meaning clearly, including the use of a capital letter at the beginning of a sentence and the appropriate punctuation mark at the end

title.name: Title
title.value: Comprehension: Understanding and Responding to Texts

content.name: Content
content.value: apply foundational knowledge and skills to understand a variety of texts, including digital and media texts, by creators with diverse identities, perspectives, and experience, and demonstrate an understanding of the patterns, features, and elements of style associated with various text forms and genres

title.name: Title
title.value: Using Foundational Knowledge and Skills to Comprehend Texts

content.name: Content
content.value: read and comprehend short, simple texts, using knowledge of words, grammar, cohesive ties, sentence structures, and background knowledge

content.name: Content
content.value: identify simple literary and informational text forms and their associated genres

content.name: Content
content.value: identify some text patterns, such as sequencing and chronological order, and text features, including illustrations, symbols, and titles, associated with various text forms, and explain how they help readers, listeners, and viewers understand the meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between simple illustrations, images, and graphics and the text

title.name: Title
title.value: Indigenous Context of Various Text Forms

content.name: Content
content.value: read, listen to, and view various forms of texts by diverse First Nations, Métis, and Inuit creators to demonstrate understanding of various aspects of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit histories, cultures, relationships, communities, groups, nations, and lived experiences

content.name: Content
content.value: apply comprehension strategies before, during, and after reading, listening to, and viewing a variety of texts, including digital and media texts, by creators with diverse identities, perspectives, and experience, in order to understand and clarify the meaning of texts

content.name: Content
content.value: activate prior knowledge, including knowledge gained from personal and text experiences, that they can use to understand the topics of new texts

title.name: Title
title.value: Prereading: Identifying the Purpose for Reading, Listening, and Viewing

content.name: Content
content.value: identify purposes for engaging with texts, including enjoyment or finding information

title.name: Title
title.value: Summarizing: Identifying Relevant Information and Drawing Conclusions

content.name: Content
content.value: identify important information in a simple text, including the main idea

content.name: Content
content.value: identify strategies, such as activating prior knowledge and visualizing, that have helped them comprehend texts

content.name: Content
content.value: apply critical thinking skills to deepen understanding of texts, and analyze how various perspectives and topics are communicated and addressed in a variety of texts, including digital, media, and cultural texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify simple literary devices, including rhyme, alliteration, and onomatopoeia, and describe how they help communicate meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: make simple inferences, using stated and implied information and ideas, to understand simple texts

content.name: Content
content.value: analyze simple texts, including literary and informational texts, by identifying and sequencing important information and events

content.name: Content
content.value: identify some cultural elements represented in various texts, including symbols and values, and explain how these elements contribute to the meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: identify thinking skills that helped them understand simple texts

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate a personal voice in their texts, with a focus on using words that express their thoughts, feelings, and opinions about the topic

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the point of view, including first person, used in their texts

content.name: Content
content.value: make simple edits to draft texts, such as changes to capitalization, punctuation, and spelling

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the forms, conventions, and techniques of digital and media texts, and apply this understanding when analyzing texts

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the interrelationships between the form, message, and context of a text, the audience, and the creator

content.name: Content
content.value: use digital and media tools to support stages of the design process and to develop creative solutions to authentic, real-world problems

content.name: Content
content.value: communicate and collaborate with various communities in a safe, respectful, responsible, and inclusive manner when using online platforms and environments, including digital and media tools, and demonstrate cultural awareness with members of the community

content.name: Content
content.value: apply the knowledge and skills developed in this grade to support learning in various subject areas and identify some ways this learning can be used in everyday life

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the contributions, lived experiences, and perspectives of a diversity of individuals and communities, including those in Canada, by exploring the concepts of identity, self, and sense of belonging in culturally responsive and relevant texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify and use oral and non-verbal communication strategies, including expression, gestures, and body language, to interpret or contribute to the meaning of messages

title.name: Title
title.value: Word Choice, Syntax, and Grammar in Oral Communication

content.name: Content
content.value: use appropriate word choice, including new vocabulary, grammar, and cohesive phrases and sentences when speaking and communicating ideas

content.name: Content
content.value: identify some simple elements of style in texts, including voice, word choice, word patterns, and sentence structure, and describe how they help communicate meaning

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the narrator’s point of view in a variety of texts, and suggest an alternative point of view to tell the story

title.name: Title
title.value: Monitoring of Understanding: Making and Confirming Predictions

content.name: Content
content.value: make predictions using background knowledge, text features, and evidence from the text

title.name: Title
title.value: Monitoring of Understanding: Ongoing Comprehension Check

content.name: Content
content.value: use strategies such as rereading, visualizing, and asking questions, to monitor their understanding of simple texts

content.name: Content
content.value: identify connections between ideas expressed in simple texts and their knowledges and lived experiences, the ideas in other familiar texts, and the world around them

content.name: Content
content.value: identify explicit and implicit perspectives communicated in a text, and describe how these perspectives could influence an audience

content.name: Content
content.value: express personal thoughts and feelings about ideas presented in texts, such as ideas about diversity, inclusion, and accessibility

content.name: Content
content.value: identify some ways in which texts created by First Nations, Métis, and Inuit individuals, communities, groups, or nations communicate about historical periods, cultural experiences, and events, and how they relate to current lived experiences

title.name: Title
title.value: Composition: Expressing Ideas and Creating Texts

content.name: Content
content.value: plan, develop ideas, gather information, and organize content for creating texts of various forms, including digital and media texts, on a variety of topics

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the topic, purpose, and audience for various simple texts they plan to create

content.name: Content

content.name: Content
content.value: gather information and content relevant to a topic, using a single source

content.name: Content

content.name: Content

content.name: Content

content.name: Content
content.value: print letters and words with appropriate formation patterns, size, placement, and spacing

content.name: Content

content.name: Content
content.value: identify a strategy they found helpful when presenting texts
